text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italian president Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, on a visit to Berlin, said that in order for Italy to join the first wave of EMU structural reforms of the welfare state were needed as soon as possible (all).

* Hard left Communist Refoundation president Armando Cossutta harshly criticised Scalfaro's comments, saying he should not get involved with economic or political debate over reforms in the welfare system, the matter was in fact up to the government and to the parliament (all).

* About 150 Italian troops from a multinational security forces landed by sea in the rebel-held Albanian port city of Vlore on Monday. The soldiers' mission will be to protect aid deliveries to the city. (all)
* Prime minister Romano Prodi said that Italy considered it vital for Albania's planned general election to go ahead by the end of June (all).

* Consumer price index as shown by six sample cities rose 0.3 percent month on month and 1.8 percent year on year in April, the lowest level since 1969. Prodi praised the figures saying they were a sign of the Italian economy's revived energy (all).

* In an interview, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said he was very satisfied with yesterday's inflation results, considering there would now be room for a rate cut. The ministry added that positive data could even win the approval of hard left opposition and persuade them pensions reform was necessary (Corriere della Sera)

* State-controlled telecoms group STET said it had agreed a co-operattion telecoms deal with Spanish electricity group Endesa and Union Fenosa. A joint statement added that STET, Endesa and Union Fenosa will also take part in a privatisation bid for Spanish television company Retevision (Sole 24 Ore).
* The Agnelli familiy-owned financial groups of Ifi and Ifil will sell a 2.2 percent stake in car giant Fiat to banking group Istituto San Paolo di Torino by mid-january 1998 (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
